blocks.text: Japan’s iconic Mt. Fuji got its first snowcap of the season on Friday, the Japan Meteorological Agency said, with radar and other data being used instead of visual observations for the first time. The confirmation came 28 days later than average and seven days later than last year, although the change in methods makes a direct comparison difficult. The new methods introduced this season, also employing the Himawari weather satellite, are aimed at improving accuracy and reducing workloads, an official of the agency’s local observatory in Yamanashi Prefecture said.
